124	## Worktree and environment mechanics
125	
126	- Work in a second worktree sharing the same `.git`:
127	  `git worktree add ../fortress-clean a874948ac` then
128	  `cd /home/user/fortress-clean && git checkout -b clean-ladder`.
129	  The session cwd stays `/home/user/fortress`; the working-branch checkout
130	  is never disturbed mid-gate.
131	- All builds/gates run with `FORTRESS_HOME=/home/user/fortress-clean` and
132	  `unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS`. Env vars do not persist between shell calls —
133	  export them inside every command.
134	- JDKs (all verified installed): `/usr/lib/jvm/java-{8,11,17,21,25}-openjdk-amd64`.
135	  If the container was recycled, reinstall via
136	  `apt-get install -y openjdk-{8,11,17,21,25}-jdk-headless ant`.
137	- Disk is a fixed allowance: before starting, `ant clean` in
138	  `/home/user/fortress` and wipe its `default_repository/caches/*` to free
139	  space; do the same in the clean worktree between rungs if space runs low.
140	- Push: `git push -u origin clean-ladder` after the exhibit block, then
141	  after every gated commit (network retries per standing orders: 2s/4s/8s/16s).
142	- **Never** commit this plan, or any working-branch-only file, on
143	  `clean-ladder`. Never force-push `clean-ladder` once published except to
144	  fix a same-session mistake.
145	
146	## Orchestration (agreed with Pavol, 2026-08-23)
147	
148	Coordinator/worker split, so the coordinating session's context survives the
149	whole ladder without compaction:
150	
151	- **Coordinator** (the main session) never runs a build or reads a log dump.
152	  It sequences workers, launches them with a brief, and between workers runs
153	  cheap read-only verification: commit landed, tree matches the reference
154	  commit where this plan says it must, gate numbers as expected, checklist
155	  tick present. Deviations land with the coordinator; anything in "Known
156	  risks / stop conditions" goes to Pavol.
157	- **Workers** execute one step each, strictly **serially** (they share the
158	  `../fortress-clean` worktree). Each worker reads its step's section of
159	  this file directly — briefs point at the plan by reference (step ID, this
160	  file's path, worktree path, env constants, commit footer), they do not
161	  paraphrase it. Each worker: executes, verifies its own results, writes
162	  the commit(s) on `clean-ladder`, pushes at this plan's push points, ticks
163	  its checkbox in the Execution checklist below, commits that tick on the
164	  working branch, and reports back tersely (SHA, verification numbers,
165	  deviations).
166	- **Granularity**: E1–E6 and C1 are done inline by the coordinator (no
167	  builds, but concentrated fiddly judgment — cherry-pick conflict
168	  resolution, README edits); B1–B8 and R1–R8 get one worker per gated
169	  commit (the build/gate log volume is exactly what would force coordinator
170	  compaction).
171	- **Two branch tracks, never mixed**: rebuild commits exist only on
172	  `clean-ladder` (pushed to `origin/clean-ladder`; Pavol renames via the
173	  GitHub UI at the end; `main` is never touched from the clean worktree).
174	  Checklist ticks are working-branch commits in `/home/user/fortress` on
175	  `claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr` — the ff-main standing order
176	  (`explorations/protocol.md` §4) applies to those pushes only.
177	
178	## Gate definitions

180	- **Full gate**: `ant clean compileAll` + `ant testFast` + `ant testSystem`
181	  all green on the stated JDK, run in the clean worktree.
182	- **Cheap gate**: `ant compileAll` + `ant testFast` (used only where stated).
